Subject: Reseller sandbox deploy checklist: pgvector + S3 integration

Hi Jordan —

Following up from last week's call — I put together a short checklist so ResellerCloud's sandbox can validate the pgvector + S3 fallthrough path with our runtime. Goal is a reproducible demo flow for prospects and a handoff to the technical onboarding team. Can you confirm the target week for the sandbox window?

High-level checklist (attached runbook):
- Infra: VPC peering, Egress rules, NAT/GW inbound for test harness
- Data: S3 bucket with versioned test set, pgvector DB replica (pg13/pgvector extension)
- Redwood runtime: connector config, prefix cache enabled, fallback ordering (pgvector -> S3)
- Observability: token-level latency traces, per-route cost estimates enabled
- Security: KMS key for S3, IP allowlist for dev accounts

We attached a runbook and a diagram — Ben can answer kernel/serving tweaks, Laura will coordinate timelines with Ops. If you can share a preferred sandbox window (2x 4-hour blocks) we will slot an engineer.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Avery —

Thanks for the checklist and the runbook. Quick questions from our infra lead before we lock calendar: 
1) For the pgvector replica, do we need a specific extension/patch level (we run pg13 with pgvector 0.6.3)?
2) What are the expected read/write QPS for the demo? We planned a small load generator, want to avoid OOMs in the sandbox.
3) Can you confirm if the S3 bucket needs Object Lock enabled for the test dataset? (compliance ask from one of our customers)

We're aiming for week of June 24 for the sandbox window; prefer Thu/Fri afternoons Pacific. We can provision creds and a small staging cluster. I'll attach our infra diagram and a short CSV with the test dataset counts.

Jordan
Jordan Klein
Head of Solutions, ResellerCloud

From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Reseller sandbox deploy checklist: pgvector + S3 integration

Jordan —

Quick answers: 
- pgvector: 0.6.3 on PG13 is fine; we recommend increasing work_mem to 64MB for the demo queries. Also ensure the extension is installed on the replica and that the index uses ivfflat for our latency profiles.
- QPS guidance: for the demo keep to <= 200 QPS sustained, and 500 QPS bursts for short periods. Our default runtime bins will hold up; if you expect >500 QPS we should provision an extra worker and enable async batching.
- S3 Object Lock: not required for functional tests, but if your customer requires it, it should be fine as long as lifecycle rules don't auto-expire within the sandbox window. We do need versioning enabled so we can validate fallthrough integrity.

Operational notes: 
- Fallback ordering is configured as: primary->pgvector (low-latency) then fallback->S3 (cold retrieval). We expose a per-route switch to invert ordering for customer demos.
- Prefix caching: enable the prefix cache for repeated context across requests — it reduces token cost and improves tail latency for the demo.
- IAM: create a role with GetObject and ListBucket for the demo runner. KMS decrypt allowed for the same role.

I'll prep a short test-run script and attach a sample results matrix (s3-pgvector-fallback-matrix.xlsx).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
